scope: Two further audits of approval/content binding and remote install exit acknowledgment

focus: Private ZIP member names and duplicate entries
Native package identity versus reviewed manifest
added_regressions: Duplicate manifest and unexpected traversal-like member rejected without writing outside private workspace
Source replaced after confirmation rejected before router inventory or upload
Both IPK and APK identity mismatch rejected

pass_two.focus: Cleanup after native package installation timeouts or connection failures
pass_two.finding: Unconditional cleanup could delete private package files while remote native installation might still need them; channel close does not acknowledge command termination
fixes: SnapshotCommandFailure preserves whether a nonzero remote exit was actually received
Installation pending state remains set on timeout, transport loss or missing exit status
Unknown installation exit retains private workspace and reports uncertainty; immediate retry discouraged
Confirmed native exit permits cleanup even if later inventory verification fails
pass_two.source_reasoning: Potential continued remote execution is an inference from the SSH/Paramiko contract, not a real-router reproduction or a claim that every Dropbear continues after close
added_regressions: Known nonzero native exit cleans workspace
Lost connection during install preserves packages
Inventory timeout after acknowledged install still cleans
Existing timeout test now explicitly requires workspace retention

validation.syntax_encoding_whitespace: Changed Python files compile; UTF-8 and whitespace checks clean

limits: No real router factory-reset and offline-restore acceptance
Retained workspace occupies router /tmp when exit is unknown; do not infer installation completion or immediately rerun
No remote kill, forced rollback, restart or retry added
Debian business tests bypass capture_services initialization because PySide6 absent; no desktop UI acceptance
Previous native package and BusyBox tests were not repeated for this orchestration-only change
